title: HINT for Technical Writers — docs keep their structure
metaDescription: Keep doc types, terminology, required sections and source rules beside documentation so assistants do not invent product behavior.
h1: Your assistant writes quickly. HINT keeps the docs factual and complete.
intro: HINT keeps plain-text rules for document types, terminology, sections and samples beside the docs. Your assistant reads the rules for this page before writing, including where product facts must come from.

situations.before: A tutorial includes a plausible CLI flag that does not exist.
situations.body: Commands, fields and defaults must come from declared product material; unknown behavior is marked to confirm.

situations.before: A reference page ships without a required section.
situations.body: The page inherits the section checklist for its type, and the emit pack can create the skeleton before anyone writes prose.

situations.before: The same feature gets three names across a doc set.
situations.body: Preferred terminology and banned variants travel with every page in the relevant documentation area.

example.intro: The Pied Piper docs demo grounds its tutorial page in an approved product source.
example.after: It builds the required tutorial sections, uses the approved terminology, and marks any missing product fact instead of creating a flag or default.
example.compiled:
<page name="tutorials-1">
  Approved page grounded in SRC-1.
</page>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent a CLI flag, API field, default or product behavior.
Omit a required section for the declared document type.
Publish a code sample that has not met the declared runnable-sample policy.
disclaimer: HINT keeps writing constraints visible; product owners and reviewers still approve factual accuracy and publication readiness.

faq.a: No. Vale checks prose rules mechanically; HINT supplies page-specific structure, facts and intent to the assistant before prose exists.
Yes. Where the Markdown emit pack applies, it can write required headings and leave constrained holes for authored content.

faq.q: Can different doc types have different rules?
faq.a: Yes. Tutorial, how-to, reference and explanation folders can inherit distinct structure and sample policies.

keywordDescriptions.docset: Defines the documentation collection and its audience.
keywordDescriptions.doctype: Declares the page type and the sections it requires.
keywordDescriptions.page: Names a page and the purpose its H1 must express.
keywordDescriptions.section: Requires a particular section in the document.
keywordDescriptions.procedure: Structures an ordered task for a reader.
keywordDescriptions.snippet: Sets the language and verification rule for a code sample.
keywordDescriptions.banned: Lists wording that must not appear.
keywordDescriptions.locale: Sets language and regional conventions for a page.
